third_difference_disposition.statement: No complete axis-aligned three-oddness E/O cube exists inside the observed repaired structural class carriers, so the naive eight-corner third-difference construction is structurally non-discriminating rather than evidence against cubic interaction.

findings.statement: The observed repaired-coordinate carriers contain no complete axis-aligned E/O 3-cubes at fixed descriptor presence, so direct third finite differences cannot expose the cubic law without matched realizable relations.

Fixed-presence oddness states occupy thin affine/non-coordinate fibers with additional linear constraints beyond width parity on almost every observed fiber; arbitrary independent toggling of three oddness coordinates is not a lawful local model of the reachable quotient.

The image of the deterministic degree<=2 left-kernel under the complete OOO map has ranks 75, 294, and 16, exactly reproducing the independently measured oddness-only cubic rank gains on 6x3-k3, 4x5-k4, and 6x3-k4.

The scalar dependency residue factors through the OOO structural residue quotient on all three hard carriers: every zero OOO residue has zero scalar residue, and a structurally selected OOO-residue basis preserves scalar image dimensions 1, 2, and 2.

On 4x5-k4 the 371-dimensional full cubic correction space decomposes into a 294-dimensional OOO image plus a 77-dimensional kernel invisible to OOO. This 77-dimensional kernel matches the earlier 77 presence-containing cubic quotient directions and is scalar-null under the OOO-exact decoder.

nonclaims: Individual matched dependencies are deterministic basis representatives, not canonical minimal circuits.
Individual OOO triples or coefficients are not promoted as invariant syndrome terms.
The 77-dimensional kernel statement is a quotient-dimension identity in the tested 4x5-k4 structural matrix, not a universal theorem.
EW-RS-059 PRIMARY 3x6-k4 and BACKUP 5x3-k4 remain sealed.
No Q-A/Q-F, standard-7x6 sufficiency, universal cubic sufficiency, or center-opening proof follows.
